before_messages.content: How can I take a picture of my whole screen on my Windows 11 computer?

You can use **Snipping Tool**.

1. Select **Start**, type **snipping tool**, then select **Snipping Tool**.
2. Select **Snipping Mode**, then choose **Full screen**.
3. Select **New**.

It captures the whole screen right away.
OK it took the picture but I can't tell where it went. How do I find it?

Snips are saved automatically in your **Screenshots** folder.

1. Open **File Explorer** from the taskbar.
2. On the left side, select the **Pictures** folder, then select **Screenshots**.
3. If you want another copy somewhere else, select **Save as** in Snipping Tool, choose a location and a name, then select **Save**.

To change where snips are saved, select **See More** in Snipping Tool, then **Settings**.

before_messages.content: I haven't used my Gmail on the computer in ages because my phone just stays logged in, but my phone broke and now the new one is asking for the password and I have no idea what it is.

That happens a lot when a phone stays signed in for years. You can get back in through Google's account recovery. It usually takes a few minutes.

1. Go to **accounts.google.com/signin/recovery** (Google's account recovery page).
2. Answer the questions it asks to show the account is yours. Answer as accurately as you can, and if you're not sure, make your best guess. A wrong guess doesn't end the process, and you can try again.
3. When asked, create a **new password** that you haven't used for this account before.

**Stay safe while you do this:**
- Google staff can't help you sign in over the phone, so ignore anyone who calls or messages offering to recover your account.
- Never share your password or any verification code with anyone.

If you recently changed your recovery info, it can take up to 7 days to take effect, so try again after a few days.

before_messages.content: I get a lot of spam calls from numbers I don't know. Can I make my iPhone only ring for people in my contacts?

iPhone can silence calls from numbers that aren't in your contacts and send them to voicemail. It takes about a minute.

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Apps**, then **Phone**.
3. Scroll to **Screen Unknown Callers** and tap it.
4. Choose **Silence**.

Calls from people in your contacts will still ring normally. Unknown callers go to voicemail, so check your voicemail now and then in case a doctor's office or pharmacy calls from a new number.

Tip: save important numbers, like your doctor and pharmacy, to your contacts so they always ring through.

before_messages.content: Can my Google Pixel phone filter out spam calls automatically?

The Phone app on your Pixel can filter spam calls. It takes about a minute to turn on.

1. Open the **Phone** app.
2. Tap **More options**.
3. Tap **Settings**.
4. Tap **Caller ID and spam**.
5. Make sure **See caller ID & spam** is on.
6. Turn on **Filter spam calls**.

You won't get missed call or voicemail notifications for filtered calls, but they still show in your call history, and you can still check your voicemail.

If you don't see **Filter spam calls**, your phone may use **Call Screen** instead, where spam blocking is one of the options. Tell me and I'll walk you through it.

before_messages.content: My iPhone is on silent almost all the time because I can't stand the noise. But I have a heart pill I must take at noon and I need the reminder to actually make a sound anyway. Can a reminder be loud even on silent? I want one for today at noon.

Yes, you can mark a reminder as **Urgent**. Urgent alarms sound even when your iPhone is silenced. This needs **iOS 26.2 or later** and iCloud Reminders turned on.

1. Open the **Reminders** app.
2. Tap **+ New Reminder** and type **Take heart pill**.
3. Tap the **Date and Time** button, then tap **Custom** and choose today at **12:00 PM**.
4. Tap the reminder, then tap **Info**.
5. Turn on **Urgent** under **Date & Time**.
6. Then open **Settings**, tap **Apps**, tap **Reminders**, and under **Allow Reminders to Access** turn on **Alarms**.

Urgent alarms only sound on the iPhone that Find My uses as your location.

before_messages.content: I sold my old camera online and the buyer mailed me a check for more than the price. He wants me to send him back the extra. Is that okay?

Please do not send him anything. This is a common trick: the extra money is the bait, and the check is likely fake.

1. Do not accept a check for more than the selling price.
2. Do not send back the difference, by any method.
3. Fake checks can look real, even to bank workers, and it can take weeks for a bank to find the fraud.
4. Report it to the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov.

If the check was already deposited, remember that seeing the money in your account does not mean the check is good. If it is fake, you may have to repay the bank.
